toolStatus: Primary pages I could not find or open: From The Garage and BBC Radio 1 (La Dispute), The Scenestar 2007 (The National), The Face (SOPHIE), NME (underscores), the Pitchfork 'Perfect 10' video (Wolf Alice), Sun 13 / The Beijinger / Vice (Xiu Xiu), Consequence (Alex G), GRAMMY.com and FADER (Arca), and the Red Bull Music Academy lecture (Arcade Fire/Neutral Milk Hotel). Not exhausted: Xiu Xiu, Alex G and Arca had only one search each for the whole group of links, so they are not-found for now rather than ruled out. Searches returned a lot of duplicate Qobuz and Songkick pages, which wasted results.

la-dispute>refused.note: Two searches covering From The Garage (13 Dec 2010) and the BBC Radio 1 piece. Neither page appeared. 'Influences from post-hardcore bands like Thursday, Refused, At the Drive-In and Glassjaw' shows up only on third-party pages: a Spanish listings site (conciertos.club) and, for Refused and At the Drive-In, a Melkweg gig blurb and a Phoenix New Times piece ('you get echoes of...'), which are critic comparisons, not La Dispute's own words.

la-dispute>at-the-drive-in.note: Same two searches as the Refused link. An NPR All Songs Considered piece (2011) says La Dispute has 'all the hooks of a pop-punk band raised on At the Drive-In', which is the writer's line from an email interview with Dreyer (npr.org/sections/allsongs/2011/08/23/139855535/la-dispute-half-spoken-explosions). I did not read the Dreyer answers in full, so it is unconfirmed; check that page for a Dreyer quote.

la-dispute>modest-mouse.note: BBC Radio 1 'Under the Influence with La Dispute' (Joanna Newsom, The Mountain Goats, Modest Mouse) did not come up in two searches.

mitski>bjork.found: She cites the international folk music her dad would play, and the Japanese pop her mom would sing to herself as inspirations, but she also draws influence from M.I.A., Mica Levi, Björk and J-pop singer Shiina Ringo, “because they all do what the fuck they want, and do it well.”
mitski>bjork.citation: Kory Grow reports in Rolling Stone (Feb 2015, '10 New Artists You Need to Know') that Mitski draws influence from Björk, among others, "because they all do what the fuck they want, and do it well."
mitski>bjork.note: The Skinny story with the record-store listening-station detail was not found. The Mitski Wikipedia page lists Björk with footnote Talbot2019, which I did not follow.

patti-smith>bob-dylan.found: During a severe bout with the flu as a teen, Smith's mother introduced her to another companion — a Dylan record. "It immediately spoke to me," Smith says, "and I became overjoyed to find this person, and I have been overjoyed ever since."
patti-smith>bob-dylan.citation: Patti Smith to Tracey Tanenbaum, NPR's Intersections (12 April 2004), on hearing Dylan as a teenager: "It immediately spoke to me, and I became overjoyed to find this person, and I have been overjoyed ever since."
patti-smith>bob-dylan.note: The PBS American Masters (1997) page and the SPIN piece in the old citation were not checked. This NPR page also says she credits her sound to lessons from Rimbaud and Dylan.

sophie>depeche-mode.note: Two searches. The Face (2017) page did not come up. An NPR World Cafe piece mentions a 2020 interview with The Face in which SOPHIE named a different song (a Malice and Pusha T hit) as formative; it does not mention Depeche Mode, and I could not open the Face piece. 'Just Can't Get Enough' is a 1981 single, so check the year against whatever source is found.

the-national>violent-femmes.note: Two searches for The Scenestar (2007, Cheryl Cheng). The page did not come up. A fan blog (philnel.com, 'Where Is My Mind?: The National's Influences') quotes the line 'The bands that I first really started falling in love with were The Smiths, Violent Femmes, Tom Waits, Nick Cave...' and credits it to a 2007 interview, but that is a secondary page. A Far Out piece says Berninger's 'Kiss Off' (Violent Femmes) is among songs that 'made me want to do it'; I did not open it.

the-national>nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds.found: I mean, I’ve been a huge fan of people like Tom Waits and Leonard Cohen and The Smiths and Nick Cave, and so I was obsessed with sort of lyric heavy writers. Neil Young and Bob Dylan, those kinds of guys.
the-national>nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds.citation: Matt Berninger to Jesse Thorn, The Sound of Young America (21 Nov 2010): "I’ve been a huge fan of people like Tom Waits and Leonard Cohen and The Smiths and Nick Cave, and so I was obsessed with sort of lyric heavy writers."
the-national>nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds.note: The Scenestar 2007, Q at Reading 2011 and 2023 talk named in the old citation were not found.

the-national>joy-division.note: Two searches. The Scenestar page did not come up. A fan blog (philnel.com/?p=2813, 'Where Is My Mind?: The National's Influences') quotes Berninger: 'Definitely Joy Division, I know Bryan our drummer, from a drumming perspective, that’s been a big influence on him.' It is a secondary source without a visible original; the line may come from The Scenestar.

the-national>nirvana.note: Two searches. The Q 2011 fan transcription did not appear. In the Sound of Young America interview Berninger mentions Nirvana only to say 'I don’t think we’re nearly as dark as, say, Nirvana', which is not influence. A fan blog quotes him saying the Strokes have influenced more bands than 'the artists I mentioned [Waits, Cave, Nirvana, Smiths]', but I could not trace it to a primary page.

underscores>oklou.note: Two searches for the NME 2026 piece. Not found. A Dazed article lists 'Harvest Sky' as an Oklou/underscores collaboration, which is a collaboration and does not count.

wolf-alice>the-replacements.note: One search for the Pitchfork 'Perfect 10' video. No Pitchfork page or transcript came up, so the 'super influential to me' line is unconfirmed.

wolf-alice>yeah-yeah-yeahs.found: Kings Of Leon, Pixies, Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Queens Of The Stone Age, Patrick Wolf and a pint of turbo shandy.
wolf-alice>yeah-yeah-yeahs.citation: Ellie Rowsell to The Line of Best Fit (6 June 2013), asked who or what had the biggest influence on the band's sound: "Kings Of Leon, Pixies, Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Queens Of The Stone Age, Patrick Wolf and a pint of turbo shandy."
wolf-alice>yeah-yeah-yeahs.note: The old citation had no quote. A 2026 Marie Claire profile also quotes Rowsell saying 'I loved the Yeah Yeah Yeahs growing up, and I think Karen O is one of our best rock stars'; I saw it only in a search result.

xiu-xiu>joy-division.note: One search for the group of four Xiu Xiu links, aimed at the Sun 13 quote. The Knife Play sticker was not found. Not exhausted.

xiu-xiu>cocteau-twins.note: One search ('4AD records like Bauhaus, This Mortal Coil, Cocteau Twins' Sun 13). The Sun 13 (2024) page did not come up. Not exhausted.

xiu-xiu>swans.note: Not searched separately; the single Xiu Xiu search did not surface The Beijinger (2014). Try a direct search for the Jamie Stewart/Michael Gira Beijinger piece.

xiu-xiu>nico.note: Not searched separately. Try the Vice page on Angel Guts: Red Classroom (a mean, tight hearted, blackness of Neubauten vs Suicide vs Nico). Note this quote describes the album's sound, not necessarily an influence statement.

alex-g>elliott-smith.note: One search for the Consequence (2015) 'Ruining Alex G' piece and the OndaRock quote; neither came up. Wikipedia's Alex G page says Smith 'is an influence of his' with no usable footnote found here. Not exhausted.

arca>squarepusher.note: One search for GRAMMY.com and FADER. Neither page came up. Wikipedia's Arca page says her childhood listening to her brother's music (Aphex Twin, Squarepusher, Björk) was an influence, with footnote [8] I did not follow. Not exhausted.

arca>autechre.note: One search for the FADER 2014 piece. Not found. Not exhausted.

arcade-fire>neutral-milk-hotel.note: One search for the Red Bull Music Academy lecture; the page did not come up. A Treble piece and a Popshifter piece say Butler signed to Merge partly because it was Neutral Milk Hotel's label, which is a label reason, not an influence statement.
